title: Russian Jet-Powered Drone Strikes Odesa–Dnipro Passenger Train, Killing Driver and Assistant
detail: A Russian jet-powered Shahed-type drone struck the locomotive of the Odesa–Dnipro passenger train near Berezivka in Odesa oblast on the morning of August 13. A monitoring team had detected the drone and ordered the train to stop, but the drone's sudden maneuver left the crew too little time to evacuate after stopping. The 50-year-old driver and his 41-year-old assistant were killed. All 340 passengers, including 67 children, were evacuated safely and bused to Odesa. President Zelensky said the strike targeted "a clearly civilian object" and that the drone operator could not have been unaware of that.

title: Ukraine Strikes Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat Refinery in Bashkortostan for Second Time in a Month
detail: Ukraine's Defense Forces, including operators from the 1st Separate Center of the Unmanned Systems Forces, struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Salavat, Bashkortostan — roughly 1,300km from the Ukrainian border — on the night of August 13, igniting a fire. It was the second hit on the facility in a month, following a July 14 strike that damaged two primary distillation units. The refinery processes around 7.2 million tons of crude annually (~2.7% of Russia's refining capacity). The strike compounds a wave of Ukrainian attacks that has pushed Russian oil refining to its lowest level since 2002, triggering fuel shortages across at least 16 Russian regions.
